authority_statement: Informational report only; the deterministic LFighter pipeline retains all security decision authority.
executive_summary: Observed DDoS-to-Benign prediction rates were higher in the plain attack branch than in the paired clean branch; the defended rate was lower than the plain attack rate. Reconstruction reduced normalized attribution distance to the paired preattack clean reference, without establishing oracle clean recovery.

facts.statement: The plain attack mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.191026, versus 0.056499 in the paired clean branch.
The defended mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.094131, an absolute reduction of 0.096894 from the plain attack branch.
Mean and minimum malicious recall were 1.000000; maximum benign false-positive rate was 0.100000.
Normalized attribution distance decreased from 0.860237 to 0.520150, with recovery fraction 0.395341.

interpretations.statement: The observed prediction behavior is consistent with targeted suppression of DDoS predictions toward the Benign class, but does not establish malicious intent.
Reconstruction moved the attribution profile toward its paired preattack clean reference; this is not evidence of oracle clean restoration.

refusals: Refused to assert malicious intent: it is unsupported by the evidence.
Refused to claim oracle clean recovery: oracle-clean attribution state was unavailable and recovery was measured against a paired preattack clean reference.
uncertainties: The clean attribution comparator is the paired round 4 preattack reference rather than an oracle clean state.
Rejected and oracle-clean attribution states were unavailable and were not substituted.
Per-client detector scores and numeric threshold values were not present in the selected summary artifacts.
Evidence is limited to development and validation; reserved test arrays remained closed.
